title: OBI LAUNCHES 2027 PRESIDENTIAL CAMPAIGN, DEMANDS CANDIDATE SCRUTINY
desc: Former Anambra governor Peter Obi formally began his bid for the 2027 Nigerian presidency on Friday, holding a press conference at his Onitsha residence. In the
body:
Former Anambra governor Peter Obi formally began his bid for the 2027 Nigerian presidency on Friday, holding a press conference at his Onitsha residence. In the remarks, Obi urged all presidential hopefuls to step out from behind “high walls of power” and present themselves directly to the electorate, defending their records and answering questions about their capacity to govern.

Obi, who is running with Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso as his vice‑presidential candidate, emphasized that his campaign will be conducted personally across Nigeria, without reliance on proxies or surrogates. He said the people deserve to hear directly from those seeking their mandate and to evaluate each candidate’s credentials, policy proposals and past performance.

The candidate highlighted a litany of challenges confronting the nation, including poverty, food insecurity, internal displacement, unemployment, weak infrastructure, unreliable electricity, and pervasive insecurity. Obi argued that Nigeria possesses the human capital, resources and market potential to overcome these hurdles, but only if leadership embraces presence, empathy and direct engagement with affected communities.

Obi outlined a development agenda focused on shifting the economy from consumption‑driven to production‑driven growth. Priorities include boosting agriculture through better security, irrigation and market access; expanding manufacturing and agro‑processing; investing in technology, construction, energy and creative industries; and improving education, vocational training, health services and maternal‑child care. He also mapped regional strengths, urging each zone to leverage its comparative advantages while contributing to a unified national economy.

The former governor called for an issue‑based campaign free of ethnic, religious or partisan propaganda, urging voters to scrutinise promises and demand evidence. He pledged that his campaign will centre on Nigerians’ urgent concerns and that the election outcome should be respected by all sides. Obi’s team plans to tour the country’s regions in the coming weeks, engaging directly with citizens to test the appeal of his “presence and empathy” narrative.

What remains to be seen is how rival candidates will respond to Obi’s challenge and whether voters will prioritize direct accountability over traditional political structures. The race is set to intensify as the 2027 election approaches, with each contender positioning themselves on the nation’s pressing economic and security agenda.

title: UBA CHAIRMAN REBUKES TRAINEE OVER FIRST-NAME GREETING
desc: A video from the United Bank for Africa's Graduate Management Accelerated Programme ceremony went viral on Thursday after a trainee greeted the group chairman,
body:
A video from the United Bank for Africa's Graduate Management Accelerated Programme ceremony went viral on Thursday after a trainee greeted the group chairman, Tony Elumelu, with Good morning, Tony. Elumelu appeared to mishear the greeting, asking Toyin?, before the trainee clarified her words. He then interrupted the session, telling her to address him as Mr Elumelu or TOE and stating he does not subscribe to that kind of Oyinbo life.

The brief exchange sparked an immediate online firestorm. Many Nigerians argued that a formal setting and the presence of the bank's chairman warranted a respectful title, while others pointed out that Elumelu has long been known by his first name in public branding and that insisting on formalities could appear out of touch. Social media users, including prominent commentators, weighed in on both sides, highlighting issues of power dynamics, generational gaps, and the practical challenges of navigating first‑name policies in corporate environments.

Commentators such as Jide Akintunde expressed surprise at Elumelu's objection, noting that the chairman’s first name has been central to his public identity for years. They suggested that a private correction would have been more appropriate and that public rebuke could be humiliating for a junior employee. Others, like Taiwo Ogunnaike, defended Elumelu, arguing that the gentle tone of the correction mitigated any disrespect and that consistency in addressing senior leaders helps maintain professional boundaries.

The debate quickly broadened beyond the single incident. Workers recalled experiences where first‑name culture was either embraced or discouraged across various Nigerian banks and multinational firms. Some highlighted inconsistencies, noting that junior staff often address senior support personnel by first name while senior executives are expected to be addressed formally. Human‑resource professionals were urged to reconsider blanket first‑name policies, citing potential mental stress for employees navigating ambiguous etiquette rules.

While the conversation continues to evolve on social platforms, corporate leaders and HR departments are now facing pressure to clarify or revise their naming conventions. The incident underscores a larger cultural negotiation: how Nigerian workplaces can integrate global, informal practices without eroding traditional respect for hierarchy. As the discussion unfolds, observers will watch for any formal statements from UBA or industry bodies that could set new standards for workplace address.

What remains unclear is whether UBA will issue an official guideline on titles and whether other Nigerian corporations will follow suit. The outcome could shape future interactions between senior executives and emerging talent across the nation.

title: Google Gives Nigerian Students Free AI
desc: Google announced on Thursday that it will provide eligible Nigerian tertiary students with a free 12‑month subscription to its Gemini AI Plus service, a package
body:
Google announced on Thursday that it will provide eligible Nigerian tertiary students with a free 12‑month subscription to its Gemini AI Plus service, a package valued at roughly ₦92,400 per user. The offer, dubbed the Gemini Student Offer, is aimed at students aged 18 and above who are enrolled in accredited universities, polytechnics or colleges of education. Those who participated in the program during the previous academic year may renew their access after confirming their student status.

The subscription unlocks a suite of advanced artificial‑intelligence tools through the Gemini app, including higher usage limits, Gemini Omni, Gemini Live for real‑time voice conversations, Deep Research for project work, custom practice quizzes, unlimited file uploads and 400 GB of cloud storage. Google says the initiative is part of a broader rollout across 27 Sub‑Saharan African countries, with Nigeria among the first to benefit.

Olumide Balogun, Google’s Director for West and East Africa, emphasized that the move is intended to remove financial obstacles and help Nigeria’s young, entrepreneurial population leapfrog into the AI era. He noted that the free year‑long access is the second consecutive year Google is offering the service at no cost, aiming to help students master complex subjects, build in‑demand digital skills and compete globally.

Google also highlighted that the program is designed to support learning rather than facilitate academic dishonesty. The Gemini platform’s Guided Learning mode acts as a tutor, offering hints and prompting questions instead of delivering direct answers. title: ARSENAL RELEASES 2026/27 SQUAD NUMBERS
desc: Arsenal announced its official jersey numbers for the 2026‑27 Premier League season on Tuesday, publishing the details on the club’s website. The release comes
body:
Arsenal announced its official jersey numbers for the 2026‑27 Premier League season on Tuesday, publishing the details on the club’s website. The release comes after a wave of transfers that reshaped the squad, with several veteran players departing and new signings arriving.
Among the newcomers, Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes has been allocated the No 39 shirt, a number he has traditionally worn in tribute to his father’s taxi licence. Greek forward Christos Tzolis receives the No 17 jersey, previously associated with former Arsenal players Oleksandr Zinchenko, Alexis Sanchez and Emmanuel Petit. French goalkeeper Illan Meslier is set to wear No 30, a number last worn by Raheem Sterling in the 2024‑25 season.
The club noted that the exits of Jakub Kiwior, Christian Norgaard and Leandro Trossard have left the numbers 15, 16, 19 and 18 vacant. Additionally, numbers 25 through 28 have not been assigned for the past two seasons, reflecting the fluid nature of squad composition.
The full roster of numbers confirms the presence of key figures such as goalkeeper David Raya (1), defender William Saliba (2), midfielder Martin Ødegaard (8) and striker Gabriel Jesus (9). Young talents like Bukayo Saka (7) and Ethan Nwaneri (18) remain central to the club’s plans, while seasoned professionals including Kai Havertz (21) and Declan Rice (27) round out the squad.
Arsenal’s statement emphasized that the new numbering scheme honors the club’s history while accommodating fresh faces, hinting at a blend of continuity and renewal for the upcoming campaign. The team will debut the new kits when the Premier League kicks off in August, and fans can expect the updated merchandise to hit stores shortly thereafter.
What remains to be seen is how the assigned numbers will translate into on‑field roles and whether the squad’s composition will deliver the title‑challenging performances the club aims for this season.
